Renew Ember's sign-in only when Copilot can switch to the new token at once
Renew Ember's sign-in when the computer wakes, instead of hours after it ran out

items.how: Reproduced: GrantKeeper.renew (auth.ts:468-494 at bbe8ab2) renewed and saved first, then switchWhenIdle waited for idle (or FORCE_BEFORE_MS) before reconnecting, so Copilot and the host's own relaunches (lost/retryLater/tasks-available, all this.token) held a token GitHub revokes at the renewal. Fixed in app/main/agent/auth.ts: new private due(grant) decides WHEN to renew (renewal time reached AND (agent idle OR now >= expiresAt - 2 min)); until then the old, still-valid token stays and nothing is renewed (30 s idle checks). renew() then calls renewGrant, track(next) and d.reconnect(next.token) with no await in between (main's reconnect sets currentToken and AgentHost.start->launch sets this.token synchronously, so host relaunches use the new token; no AgentHost.useToken needed since no gap remains), and only then saves. switchWhenIdle removed. New renewed() shares one renewGrant per refresh token between the timer and freshen (Check again during a renewal no longer spends the refresh token twice). Comments updated in main.ts keeper wiring and host.ts idle getter. The reviewer's scratch repro xreview-revoke now prints 'minutes Copilot kept the revoked token after the renewal: 0' (was 41).
items.test: test/unit/token-renewal.test.ts: 'renews only when it can switch: not while something is under way...' and 'renews anyway just before the old token runs out, and switches at once...' (the two tests that pinned the old wait, rewritten to assert no GitHub call while busy), 'never leaves Copilot on a token the renewal revoked' (pretend GitHub revoking OLD at renewal, task busy 40 min; asserts zero checks on a revoked token, including at save time), 'asks GitHub once when Check again comes during a renewal'. All four failed on bbe8ab2's keeper and pass now.

items.how: Reproduced: track() armed one monotonic setTimeout for expiresAt-1h; nothing re-armed it from the wall clock and main's resume hook only called agent.networkChanged. Fixed: GrantKeeper.after() caps every wait at RECHECK_MS = 5 min (due() re-arms when early), so a wake nobody reported is noticed within 5 min; new GrantKeeper.wake() re-checks at once (main.ts: powerMonitor 'resume' now calls keeper.wake() then agent.networkChanged(true); new powerMonitor 'unlock-screen' -> keeper.wake()); a token past its end is renewed and switched to at once regardless of work under way. New GrantKeeper.refused(token): main's onStatus, on error/sign-in for currentToken, now also calls keeper.refused(currentToken); if that is Ember's own tracked grant and its renewal time has come, it is renewed now and Copilot reconnected; a refusal of a token with more than an hour left stands (account lost Copilot), so no loop. The reviewer's xreview-suspend repro now prints 'renew calls: 1 reconnected: 1 inUse is old: false' (was 0 / true).
items.test: test/unit/token-renewal.test.ts: 'renews at once when the computer wakes past the renewal time', 'looks at the clock again every few minutes, so a wake it wasn't told about is noticed too', 'renews when Copilot refuses a sign-in whose renewal time has come, and leaves any other refusal alone', and main wiring 'tells the keeper when the computer wakes or Copilot refuses the sign-in in use'. All failed before (no wake/refused, no cap, main lines absent) and pass now.

items.how: Reproduced with a real TokenStore whose temp file can't be written (a directory in its place): freshen renewed, saveResult returned write-failed (ignored), logged 'auth.renewed', and resolveToken read the expired token back. Fixed at the root in TokenStore (app/main/agent/auth.ts): a private 'held' grant is set whenever a save isn't kept (no keyring, keyring refused, write failed); loadGrant returns it before reading the file until a later save is kept or clear() (sign-out). So findToken/startBrain/retrySignIn get the renewed grant as source 'stored', keeper.use(token) reads it back and keeps it alive, and a later freshen doesn't reuse the spent refresh token. freshen now saves through the store it read and logs auth.renewed with { when: 'before use', kept }. The same holds for the keeper's own renewal and the device flow when not kept.
items.test: test/unit/token-renewal.test.ts 'uses a stored sign-in renewed before use that couldn't be saved (a full or read-only disk), not the one on disk' (renewal logged with kept: write-failed, resolveToken gives NEW/stored, no second renewal 61 s later, kept alive and renewed 7 h later, forgotten at sign-out) and test/unit/auth-save.test.ts 'keeps a sign-in it couldn't write for this run, until one is written or it is cleared'. Both failed before and pass now.

items.how: Electron 44.5.0's node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:12104 has safeStorage.encryptStringAsync(plainText): Promise<Buffer>. Added SecretBox.encryptStringAsync and TokenStore.saveAsync: with the store option asyncKeyring (renamed from asyncDecrypt, since it now covers writes; main passes it on darwin only) it seals with encryptStringAsync; elsewhere it is saveResult itself, so Linux/Windows are unchanged. The sign-in being saved is given to every read meanwhile, saves are written in call order, a clear() (sign-out) or sync save during the keyring call makes the stale save write nothing ('write-failed'), and a keyring refusal keeps it for the run. GrantKeeper.renew (after the switch) and freshen use saveAsync; main's device flow sets currentToken/keeper.use before awaiting saveAsync (so a renewal of the replaced sign-in finishing meanwhile neither switches nor saves over it) and returns if currentToken changed (signed out) during the save. darwin-system's keychain child now also checks encryptStringAsync output opens with decryptString (doctor, older Ember) and decryptStringAsync, and TokenStore.saveAsync -> load through fresh async and sync stores.

fix.notes: Design choices: (1) X11's suggested AgentHost.useToken was not added: renew() now calls renewGrant -> track(next) -> reconnect(next.token) with no await between, and main's reconnect sets currentToken and AgentHost.start->launch sets host.token synchronously, so host relaunches never see the revoked token. (2) X13 is fixed at the store level (TokenStore 'held'), which also covers the keeper's and the device flow's not-kept saves: a device-flow sign-in with no keyring is now found by Check again for the rest of the run instead of signing the user out (same root cause; no other behaviour changes). (3) The refusal backstop (X12) may still show the 'Sign-in refused' status and notice briefly before the reconnect; suppressing that would need host.ts changes outside this package. (4) A renewal that completes after the user signed out or switched sign-in is dropped, as before (saving it could persist a signed-out sign-in). The MaxListenersExceededWarning on process 'exit' in the full npm test output is from other tests (no exit listeners were added here). The reviewers' scratch repros xreview-revoke/xreview-suspend assert the bug, so they now fail by design (they print 0 revoked minutes / renewed after wake).

problems.what: TokenStore.saveAsync (app/main/agent/auth.ts:182) still calls this.canPersist(), which runs safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable() synchronously on the main thread before encryptStringAsync. I confirmed the call order with a scratch test using a fake box that records sync calls: one saveAsync plus a fresh async load makes exactly one synchronous keyring call, isEncryptionAvailable. On macOS, Chromium's OSCrypt IsEncryptionAvailable gets the 'Safe Storage' key from the Keychain (GetEncryptionKey), and Electron's docs say 'On MacOS, returns true if Keychain is available'. Since review #241 every read in Ember's main process is async (loadGrant never calls canPersist), so this is the first synchronous keychain access of the run. Example: a user answered the post-update prompt with 'Allow' rather than 'Always Allow'. The first renewal or device-flow save can then still freeze the overlay, shortcuts and Stop on a keychain prompt, which is the case this follow-up was meant to remove. I can't prove it on Linux, and neither can the darwin-system child, which calls isEncryptionAvailable itself first.
problems.fix: On the asyncKeyring path, don't call the synchronous check. Add an optional isAsyncEncryptionAvailable?(): Promise<boolean> to SecretBox (Electron 44 has it, electron.d.ts:12135). In saveAsync, decide persistability with `await box.isAsyncEncryptionAvailable?.()` plus the basic_text check, or just let an encryptStringAsync rejection mean 'no-keyring'. Add a unit test whose isEncryptionAvailable throws on that path, and make the darwin-system keychain child call saveAsync before any synchronous safeStorage call.

problems.what: In main.ts IPC.signIn (lines 1187-1195), the device flow now sets currentToken and calls keeper.use before `await tokens?.saveAsync(grant)`, and calls agent.start only afterwards. On Linux and Windows that await is one microtask. On macOS it lasts as long as the keychain prompt. During that window: (a) Cancel is not honoured. ac.signal.aborted is not checked again after the await, so the window shows 'cancelled', then Ember connects and say() reports 'done' (signInAbort is still ac). (b) A sign-in refusal of the connection still running (the host is still on the previous token) reaches onStatus, which runs refusedTokens.add(currentToken), i.e. the NEW token. Check again then passes over the user's fresh sign-in until nothing else is left. Both cases are narrow and macOS-only, and the window is new: before, the save and the start had no gap.
problems.fix: Start the save and the connection together, so the host's token changes in the same tick as currentToken: `currentToken = token; keeper.use(token, grant); const saving = tokens?.saveAsync(grant) ?? Promise.resolve("no-keyring"); const phase = await agent?.start(token, "stored"); const kept = await saving;`. Sign-out still wins, because its agent.start(null) is queued later and clear() makes the pending save write nothing. Otherwise, at least re-check ac.signal.aborted after the await. Pin it with a main wiring test.

problems.what: The forDocs copy overstates the behaviour. The CHANGELOG bullet says Ember renews 'without cutting off what it's doing', but a task still running two minutes before the token's end is renewed anyway and cut off (FORCE_BEFORE_MS, which the item accepts). 'straight after the computer wakes from sleep' implies a renewal on every wake, but one happens only when the renewal time has passed. The README sentence starts 'Its GitHub sign-in', which is ambiguous where it would be appended.
problems.fix: Give the docs package corrected lines. CHANGELOG: '**Staying signed in**: Ember renews its GitHub sign-in by itself before it runs out, waiting where it can until it isn't in the middle of something, and as soon as the computer wakes if it ran out during sleep. ...' (rest unchanged). README: 'Ember's own GitHub sign-in lasts eight hours at a time: Ember renews it by itself before it runs out (when it isn't in the middle of something, where it can) and when the computer wakes from sleep, so you don't need to sign in again.'

verify.notes:
Code reading:
- X11: renewal waits until idle, or 2 minutes before the end. Then renew does renewed, track(next) and d.reconnect(next.token) with no await in between. main's reconnect sets currentToken, and AgentHost.start→launch sets this.token synchronously (host.ts:879-881), so lost(), retryLater/retryNow and the tasks-available relaunch use NEW from the same tick. AgentHost.useToken really isn't needed. renewed() shares one request per refresh token between the timer, refused(), wake() and freshen.
- Remaining X11 risk: one leftover race, acceptable. A slow macOS freshen read that started before a timer renewal finished can make one extra refused refresh request (it only logs auth.renew_failed; state stays correct).
- X12: every wait is capped at 5 minutes, and due() re-arms when it fires early. wake() runs on resume and unlock-screen. refused() renews only Ember's own tracked grant in its last hour or past it; one with hours left stands, so it can't loop. A 'Sign-in refused' notice can still show for up to 12 s before the reconnect when a request beats the wake renewal.
- X13: TokenStore.held, which clear() resets at sign-out, fixes it at the root for freshen, the keeper and the device flow.
- Intended side effect of X13: on Linux without a keyring, and on any failed write, Check again now finds the device-flow sign-in as 'stored' for the rest of the run. Before, it lost it.
- The device-flow's sign-out race resolves correctly: sign-out's agent.start(null) is queued last, and the epoch makes a stale save write nothing.
- Pre-existing, not this round: a renewal whose new grant lands after the keeper switched to another source is dropped unsaved. freshen covers it when findToken follows.

problems.what: Regression from the new preflight. On X11, `checks.checkTyping` (app/main/hands/borrow.ts, the new `checks` object, about line 377) runs `planText`, which plans against `x.layout()`. That reads the XKB group in effect right now (hands/input.ts layout(): XkbGetState). The preflight now runs it twice before `x.activate(o.window)`, and the worker hands it `checkTyping(text)` for type_text (non-paste), type_text into a cell and fill_cells. With GNOME's "Switch input sources individually for each window", a real option on RHEL 8, the group follows the focused window. Example: the user is in a window with a Cyrillic (or Greek, or Hebrew) layout and Ember types "hello" into a window set to US. Before this change the plan ran after the target window came to the front, so it used the US group and the typing worked. Now the preflight plans against the user's window and refuses with "The keyboard layout in use can't type “h”… Switch the layout", which is a refusal that wasn't there before and misleading advice. The same happens on macOS with "Automatically switch to a document's input source" turned on: `keyboardUsable()` there is `inputSourceReason()`, read from the user's front document instead of the target's (this hits checkTyping, and checkKeys for character keys pressed without Command, Control or Option). Repro with fakes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/relfix2-verify/lifecycle2/layout/fix.test.ts (run `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.mts` in that folder). It is a CursorBorrow whose `layout()` follows the active window (11 Cyrillic, 22 US), with `preflight: h => h.checkTyping("h")`. It fails on fix2/lifecycle2 at the preflight with that error, and the same test passed on bbe8ab2, where it typed code 43. This is the code path only: not run on a real GNOME or macOS desktop.
problems.fix: Keep the preflight to checks that don't depend on which window has the focus. On macOS (kc.os === "darwin"), skip keyboardUsable in the preflight: the input source can be per document, and the in-borrow check after activation still refuses. Alternatively, run the preflight only where the reason is the server-wide one (X11 Typing Assist). Other quote marks, quote marks set side by side (’’), and characters that show nothing or reorder text are marked in ⟨ ⟩ (⟨”⟩, ⟨’’⟩, ⟨ZWSP⟩). Text that holds quote marks says how long it is right after the quote, so typed text can't pass for Ember's own words. Reproduced on the built command page in Playwright's Chromium, at the window size main gives each text size (760x480, 874x552, 988x624). xterm's rows were 13px at all three sizes, and stayed 13px when Larger was chosen while the window was open (scratchpad/css2/term-font.mjs). The fix:
- terminal-options.ts: TERM_FONT_PX (13). textScaleOf() parses ember.css's --text-scale as getComputedStyle returns it; anything not from 1 to 2 counts as 1. termFontSize() rounds to whole px (13, 15, 17) so the cells stay sharp. terminalOptions() takes the scale.
- terminal.ts: a new terminal starts at the page's scale. setTextScale() sets term.options.fontSize, and xterm then re-measures and redraws. cellSize() measures at the scale.
- command/main.ts: a MutationObserver on html[data-text-size] (main sets it on dom-ready and whenever the setting changes) calls setTextScale on every open terminal, then reportSize(). The parts around the terminal take 250 + 105 x (scale - 1) px, fitted to measured parts of 203, 219 and 234 px at Default, Large and Larger (chrome.mjs).

A run keeps its columns and rows because its size is fixed for the run (no resize path through script, design 3.10). Its cells grow, and the window grows by the same scale (round 1).

- Fonts are 13px, 15px and 17px.

- A new run at the reported size fits with no scrolling at every size: 90x12, 91x12 and 91x13.

The new restartAfterUpdate(app, env, argv) in app/main/install-watch.ts (plain Node, Electron's app passed in through a Relauncher interface) uses admin-watch's restartOptions, the same rule the admin-policy restart already follows. Inside an AppImage it calls app.relaunch({execPath: $APPIMAGE, args: argv.slice(1)}). Everywhere else it calls app.relaunch() with no argument at all, so the RPM, Windows and macOS restarts are exactly what they were. Then it quits. main.ts's update check calls it. Caveat 1: in an AppImage the update check itself watches package.json inside the read-only mount, which can't change while Ember runs, so today this path is defensive. Caveat 2 (pre-existing and beyond this package): restartOptions, autostart.ts, the doctor probe and emberPathsOf all trust env.APPIMAGE. An RPM Ember started from a terminal inside another AppImage app inherits that app's APPIMAGE and would restart the wrong program. A possible follow-up is to honour APPIMAGE only when realpath(APPDIR) contains process.execPath.

They come after its WSL tests, which therefore still find the distro stopped with no sshd; setup-wsl's packages are unchanged. (1) pwsh: the runner's new Win32-OpenSSH key and ~/.ssh/config 'Host 127.0.0.1 / User ember' (the distro's non-root default user; the WSL1 job uses root). (2) Git Bash: wsl.exe -u root --exec /bin/bash -s with the script on stdin and $USERPROFILE as $1. It writes sshd_config.d/ember-ci.conf with 'Port 2222', installs openssh-server (so systemd's ssh.service runs on 2222), authorises the key for ember through wslpath, then runs systemctl restart ssh and systemctl is-active ssh. WSL stops a distro 15 s after its last wsl.exe ends (instanceIdleTimeout), so something must stay attached. The step then waits up to 30 s for 127.0.0.1:2222 from Windows. (4) pwsh: an accept-new batch connect, copied from the WSL1 job, that prints the user and kernel. (5) node scripts/package/remote-parts.mjs. findings.title: An unasked SSH offer can wait behind a held "Can't connect" / "Lost" bubble with no time limit, then show "You're connected to web-07" long after that ssh session ended
findings.scenario: build-01 is added. A connect fails, so "Can't connect to build-01 [Try again][Close]" is shown and held until the user closes it. The user runs `ssh deploy@web-07` in a terminal, and the noticer posts the unasked offer on the new offers board (X3 fix: claim "reply", ms OFFER_MS). The user then ends that ssh session and leaves the failure bubble up. 45 minutes later they press Close. The waiting offer then appears: "You're connected to web-07 — Bring me there too? [Bring Ember][Not now][Don't offer again]". It is untrue at that point, and it holds Ember still for 25 s (250 s with More time on). It also uses up the one offer per run for that destination, because noticer.offered was marked when the offer was posted. The same happens behind a held "Lost build-01", and with the WSL first-seen offer (line 1284).
findings.evidence: I reproduced it with a scratch vitest file that copies test/unit/targets-runtime.test.ts and adds one case. It uses the file's own screenRig/rig with both boards (bubbles + offers). The noticer sees `ssh deploy@web-07`, then userSshProcesses returns [] for 10 ticks, the test advances 45 min and presses the failure bubble's Close. Output: `SCRATCH after Close: {"title":"You're connected to web-07","thought":"Bring me there too? I'll open my own connection with your SSH settings.","actions":["Bring Ember","Not now","Don't offer again"]}` and the assertion fails. File: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/relfix2-review/tree/test/unit/xr-stale-offer.test.ts (run from that tree with `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.mts test/unit/xr-stale-offer.test.ts -t SCRATCH`). Cause in the code: showSeenOffer posts with `{ ms: OFFER_MS, claim: "reply" }` (runtime.ts:1194) to the offers board (runtime.ts:696-701). Presenter.armHide only stores pendingHide while the bubble is unseen (presenter.ts:716), so the 25 s count starts only once the offer reaches the screen, and a held bubble can keep it unseen forever. Nothing withdraws the offer when the ssh process goes away, and nothing checks again at show time. The existing X3 test ('wait behind a held "Can't connect" bubble, which stays until it is closed') only checks that the offer is still waiting after 60 s.
findings.fix: Bound how long an unasked offer may wait. Either (a) drop it when it hasn't reached the screen within OFFER_MS of being posted (or check the noticer's live ssh processes when it is about to show), and take its key out of noticer.offered so it can be offered again while the user is still connected; or (b) take X3's other suggestion: skip posting an unasked offer while a held lost:/fail:/stalled:/connecting: bubble is shown, and leave it unoffered for a later tick. Add a test where the ssh session ends before the held bubble is closed.
